input.quote: 10.5 Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed and construed and enforced in accordance with the laws of the State of New York applicable to contracts made and to be performed exclusively in that State without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
input.rationale: Section 10.5 selects New York law, which is our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement contains no dispute forum provision at all: searches for "jurisdiction", "court", "venue" and "arbitration" return no results, so no exclusive venue is designated (and no foreign arbitration seat is imposed). The preferred position requires exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, so we add that venue language to the existing sentence without disturbing the governing law choice.

ops.oldText: without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws.
ops.newText: without giving effect to the principles of conflict of laws. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement, and waives any objection to venue in such courts.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law is acceptable to us, but the clause is silent on forum, so we have added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County to match the governing law and avoid disputes over venue. We can accept Delaware or California courts as a fallback if HDI prefers.
proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County court venue to the New York governing law clause.
